newsitem.title: FRANCE: Sihanouk says Cambodia "sick man" of Asia.
newsitem.headline: Sihanouk says Cambodia "sick man" of Asia.

text.p: King Norodom Sihanouk, condemning human rights violations in Cambodia since this month's coup, has expressed fears his nation will long be the "sick man" of Asia, a Paris-based media watchdog said on Thursday.
"Alas, in Cambodia of the 1990s...recourse to armed force prevails over respect for the law," Sihanouk wrote in a letter to Reporters sans Frontieres (Reporters without Borders).
"I am very upset by such a destructive and destabilising evolution for my country, Cambodia, now considered and I fear irredeemably for many years to come as the 'sick man' of Asia," he wrote.
Sihanouk's son, Prince Norodom Ranariddh, was ousted as first prime minister in the coup by rival premier Hun Sen after two days of heavy fighting between their forces in Phnom Penh.

The letter, dated July 26 in Beijing where Sihanouk has a residence and has been undergoing medical treatment, backed Reporters sans Frontieres' denunciations of Cambodia's treatment of reporters since the coup on July 6.
Many Cambodians, including journalists, have fled or gone into hiding since the coup, fearing reprisals against those seen as having supported Ranariddh.
There have been no reports of journalists being killed since the coup, however.
Sihanouk said Cambodia's 1993 constitution meant the king had no executive power "all the more so since the events of July 5 and 6".

"I regret with all my heart the sad fate reserved to journalists and other media correspondents condemned to a certain death, or to work in conditions that are so remote from all codes of ethics or professional conduct," he wrote.
Reporters sans Frontieres wrote to Sihanouk asking for his support over the disappearance of six journalists. It said four were now "in a safe place but the situation remains worrying".
Sihanouk said in Beijing this week that he would not recognise the nomination of Foreign Minister Ung Huot as First Prime Minister, saying the position belonged to his ousted son.
